title: PineconeAI x Redwood — Beta onboarding checklist check-in
topics: Guided onboarding checklist usefulness vs confusion points
Retry/timeout guidance placement and code snippets
Prod vs test API keys and common 401s
429 rate limit/quota education step and messaging
Telemetry/validation lag and how step completion is computed
summary: PineconeAI shared beta feedback on the Console guided onboarding checklist. Overall they like having a progressive path and the deep links to docs, but several steps felt ambiguous or out of order. Biggest request: make retries/timeouts and error handling more explicit and earlier (with copy-pastable SDK snippets). They hit a few common issues (401 from wrong key environment, 429 during load tests, streaming disconnect once) and noted that checklist auto-validation sometimes lags by a few minutes, causing confusion. Redwood team committed to updating step copy, tightening definitions for “first streaming session”, and adding a clearer “production-ready defaults” section in docs/quickstarts.
next_steps: Redwood to share draft retry/timeout + error-handling doc section for review (Python/TS/Go snippets).
Redwood to propose updated checklist step ordering and revised microcopy for prod vs test keys and 429 guidance.
PineconeAI to send 2 example integration patterns (batch vs interactive streaming) so Redwood can tune checklist recommendations.
Schedule a 30-min follow-up after updated beta build ships (target next release train).
action_items: Dev Patel (Redwood): Send PineconeAI the current troubleshooting page link + internal beta feedback form by EOD 2026-02-07.
Wei Chen (Redwood): Draft updated “Retries, timeouts, and idempotency” section with SDK snippets (Python/TS/Go) by 2026-02-12.
Marissa Cole (Redwood): Review checklist step ordering and update “prod key” step description + validation expectations by 2026-02-14.
Sarah Kim (PineconeAI): Share notes on where onboarding got stuck (screenshots / step names) by 2026-02-11.
Miguel Alvarez (PineconeAI): Provide a short summary of desired SLOs (p95 latency targets, expected concurrency) to align on rate limit guidance by 2026-02-13.
transcript:
Fireflies.ai transcript

Title: PineconeAI x Redwood — Beta onboarding checklist check-in
Date: 2026-02-07
Time: 5:00pm–5:46pm PT
Duration: 46 min

Attendees
Redwood Inference: Dev Patel, Marissa Cole, Wei Chen, Priya Shah
PineconeAI: Sarah Kim, Miguel Alvarez, Jordan Lee

---

[00:00] Dev Patel: Cool. Hey Sarah, Miguel, Jordan — thanks for making the time. This is just a quick beta check-in on the new onboarding checklist in Console. We want the sharp edges.

[00:13] Sarah Kim: Yep. We’ve had like, I dunno, three people try it in the last week.

[00:18] Marissa Cole: Awesome. And just to set context, we’re mostly focused on Hosted API onboarding right now, self-serve flow. Not Dedicated/Private.

[00:26] Jordan Lee: Makes sense.

[00:28] Dev Patel: Before we get into it, any blockers right now? Like are you shipping or still evaluating?

[00:33] Miguel Alvarez: We’re still eval. We want to use Redwood for some rerank + chat in a couple internal tools. The checklist actually helped us not miss like, the usage dashboard.

[00:45] Dev Patel: Nice.

[00:47] Priya Shah: I’m here mainly for support learnings. We’ve seen a bunch of onboarding tickets around 401s and 429s.

[00:54] Sarah Kim: Yep we hit both of those, so…

[00:57] Dev Patel: Great, let’s dig in.

[01:00] Dev Patel: First question — overall usefulness from 1 to 10?

[01:05] Jordan Lee: I’d say like a 7?

[01:07] Sarah Kim: Yeah 7-ish. It’s helpful having “do these things” but a couple steps are confusing.

[01:13] Marissa Cole: Which ones?

[01:15] Sarah Kim: The “Set up prod mode key” versus “Create an API key” — we got tripped because we created a key, used it, got a 401 in one environment, and it wasn’t obvious it was because we were mixing… I guess test and prod?

[01:31] Priya Shah: Yeah that’s consistent with SUP tickets. People copy the wrong key into a server and then they get the “wrong environment” auth error.

[01:39] Miguel Alvarez: The error message was like, uh, “Unauthorized” and then some code, but we didn’t connect it to the checklist step. It didn’t say “hey you used a test key on a prod endpoint” or whatever.

[01:52] Marissa Cole: Got it. So two parts: the product error message, and the checklist microcopy.

[01:57] Dev Patel: And the step state too — did the checklist show “API key created” as completed?

[02:02] Sarah Kim: Yeah it checked it off.

[02:04] Dev Patel: But then it still showed “prod key” as incomplete, right?

[02:06] Sarah Kim: Right.

[02:08] Jordan Lee: And we weren’t sure if we needed that step for just trying it out. Like, we’re in eval mode, but we are running it in a staging service.

[02:17] Wei Chen: That’s actually a good point. The current copy assumes “prod key” means “this will be used in a production workload”, but people use staging.

[02:28] Marissa Cole: We debated calling it “Server key” vs “Production key.” But “server key” got weird.

[02:35] Miguel Alvarez: Yeah. “Prod” is okay but define it. Like, “use this for backend services, not in the browser” plus “more strict quotas” or something.

[02:46] Dev Patel: Okay.

[02:48] Dev Patel: Second — the request we heard from you async was clearer retry/timeout guidance. Want to walk through where that broke down?

[02:56] Miguel Alvarez: Yeah. So the checklist has “First request” and then later there’s a production checklist thing that mentions retries, but it’s buried. Our first integration attempt, we basically copied the snippet, and then we got intermittent timeouts. Not sure if it was network or the model, but we didn’t know what your recommended timeout is.

[03:20] Jordan Lee: And like, do we do exponential backoff? What status codes are safe to retry? If it’s streaming, do you retry the whole thing? That stuff.

[03:29] Priya Shah: The streaming piece is tricky.

[03:32] Miguel Alvarez: Exactly. And we ended up writing our own wrapper, but we wanted to just follow your “blessed path.”

[03:40] Wei Chen: When you say “copied the snippet,” was that from docs or from the checklist deep link?

[03:45] Miguel Alvarez: From the docs link the checklist sends you to. The “First request” page. It shows a minimal example, but no retries. Which is fine for hello world, but then the checklist also kinda implies you can go to production with the same code.

[04:04] Marissa Cole: That’s super fair. We tried to keep “first request” super short but we might need a “first request (production-safe defaults)” tab.

[04:13] Sarah Kim: Or just earlier in the checklist, a step that says “Add retries and timeouts” before you get to “first production launch.” Because people hit issues before they get there.

[04:26] Dev Patel: We have an internal debate on that actually — separate step vs nested under the production section.

[04:31] Jordan Lee: I’d vote separate. It’s like table stakes.

[04:36] Miguel Alvarez: Same.

[04:38] Wei Chen: Noted.

[04:40] Dev Patel: Can you describe the timeouts you saw? Like was it a 504, or the client just hung?

[04:47] Miguel Alvarez: It was client side. Node. We saw a socket hang up once. And then a request that took like 70 seconds and then our service killed it.

[04:58] Priya Shah: Was that on streaming or non-streaming?

[05:00] Miguel Alvarez: Non-streaming at first. Then we tried streaming and it felt better but we had one disconnect.

[05:08] Sarah Kim: Yeah streaming disconnect happened when we were on VPN, so could be us.

[05:14] Marissa Cole: Did the checklist mark “first streaming session” complete?

[05:18] Sarah Kim: It eventually did, but not immediately. That was another confusing thing — we finished a streaming call, came back to Console, it still said incomplete. Then like 5 minutes later it flipped.

[05:31] Marissa Cole: Okay, so validation lag. That’s expected but we should message it.

[05:37] Dev Patel: Right now it’s computed off gateway logs/metrics, not purely client-side, so there’s a delay.

[05:45] Jordan Lee: Yeah it felt like it didn’t work, so we repeated it.

[05:48] Priya Shah: Which can actually cause 429s depending on quotas.

[05:51] Sarah Kim: (laughs) yep.

[05:54] Dev Patel: That’s good feedback — we need a “this can take up to X minutes” label.

[06:00] Wei Chen: Or “refresh” and show last checked time.

[06:04] Marissa Cole: Yeah.

[06:06] Dev Patel: Let’s talk about the 429 experience. What happened there?

[06:10] Sarah Kim: We were doing a little load test, nothing crazy, like 20 concurrent calls. And then we started getting 429 and we thought it was a bug, but it was rate limit.

[06:21] Miguel Alvarez: The docs page it linked to was pretty general. It said something like “handle 429 with retries.” But it didn’t say the default limits for new accounts or where to see your quota.

[06:34] Jordan Lee: The checklist has a step “Understand rate limits and quotas” but again it’s later. Also not sure what “done” means for that step.

[06:44] Marissa Cole: Today that one is basically a deep link + manual completion. There’s no automated validation.

[06:51] Sarah Kim: Yeah, and it’s not obvious it’s manual. Like some steps auto-check when you do the thing, some you have to click.

[06:59] Dev Patel: Great callout. We’ve heard that. We might need an icon that indicates “Auto” vs “Manual.”

[07:06] Wei Chen: In docs, we can add a short “new account defaults” box but we need to make sure it’s accurate and not contractual.

[07:15] Priya Shah: Even just “you can see your current limits in Console here” would help. People don’t know where to look.

[07:22] Miguel Alvarez: Exactly.

[07:24] Dev Patel: Okay. Another thing we saw in your note was “checklist usefulness.” What did you like about it?

[07:31] Jordan Lee: Honestly the deep links were nice. We have a bunch of vendors and usually you get lost in docs. Here it’s like, click step, get the right page.

[07:41] Sarah Kim: And the “usage dashboard” step made us look at cost per token stuff earlier than we would’ve.

[07:48] Miguel Alvarez: Yeah. We also liked that it called out structured output, but we didn’t try it yet.

[07:55] Wei Chen: Was the structured output step confusing or okay?

[07:59] Miguel Alvarez: It was okay, but the step says “learn structured output basics” and I wasn’t sure if it’s required for production launch.

[08:08] Marissa Cole: It’s not required, it’s more “recommended.” We tried to keep it in the “basics” track but maybe it shouldn’t block production checklist.

[08:18] Dev Patel: Yeah, the “first production launch” definition is meant to be minimum safeguards, not features.

[08:25] Sarah Kim: I think that’s where the confusion is — the checklist mixes “things you can do” (streaming, tool calling) with “things you must do” (retries, timeouts, monitoring).

[08:38] Dev Patel: That’s a really clear framing.

[08:40] Wei Chen: We could group them. Like “Capabilities” vs “Production safety.”

[08:46] Marissa Cole: In the UI, we currently have sections but it might not be strong enough.

[08:52] Jordan Lee: Also the “First production launch” step title is a little big. Like, what is production? For us it means internal users. For you it might mean external SLA.

[09:04] Dev Patel: Totally. Our working definition is “workload where downtime or data exposure matters” — but that’s still vague.

[09:13] Priya Shah: Support’s view: production is “if you page someone when it breaks.”

[09:18] Sarah Kim: (laughs) that’s actually good.

[09:20] Marissa Cole: That’s a good heuristic.

[09:22] Dev Patel: Okay let me jump to the retry/timeout thing more specifically. If we were to add one step earlier, what would you want in it?

[09:32] Miguel Alvarez: Concrete numbers. Default timeout. Recommended retry count. Which errors to retry: 429, 500, 503. Probably not 400. And idempotency / request IDs.

[09:49] Jordan Lee: And for streaming, how to resume or whether you don’t.

[09:54] Priya Shah: We typically say don’t “resume” a partial stream — treat it as failed and re-issue, but then you need to be careful about side effects.

[10:03] Sarah Kim: Exactly. If tool calling triggers something, retrying could duplicate. So you need guidance like “only retry safe operations” or use idempotency key.

[10:14] Wei Chen: We can add a section: “If you’re using tool calls, treat requests as potentially non-idempotent and implement your own idempotency keys.” Something like that.

[10:26] Miguel Alvarez: Yep.

[10:27] Marissa Cole: Are you using Python or TS mostly?

[10:30] Miguel Alvarez: TS.

[10:31] Sarah Kim: We have some Python too.

[10:34] Wei Chen: We’ll ensure parity across TS/Python/Go. That’s the plan anyway.

[10:40] Dev Patel: Another question: the checklist has a step “first successful request.” Did that one work for you?

[10:47] Sarah Kim: It worked, but again the lag. We made the call, came back, it still said incomplete.

[10:55] Jordan Lee: We thought it was broken, so we did it again.

[10:58] Dev Patel: Yeah we should address that. Right now it’s pulling from request logs aggregated per project, so it’s not instant.

[11:07] Marissa Cole: Some steps are instant because they’re client-side events, like visiting usage dashboard.

[11:13] Sarah Kim: Which is fine, but tell the user.

[11:16] Dev Patel: Yep.

[11:18] Miguel Alvarez: Also the “first successful request” step — what’s the definition? Like, any 200? Or does it need a min token count? We saw some 200s that were like empty.

[11:31] Marissa Cole: Today it’s basically “HTTP 200 from the generate endpoint” for that project. No min tokens.

[11:39] Miguel Alvarez: Okay.

[11:40] Dev Patel: Let’s do this — I’ll recap what I’m hearing and you tell me if I missed anything.

[11:46] Dev Patel: 1) Step ordering: production safety items (timeouts/retries/monitoring) need to be more prominent / earlier. 2) Clarify “prod vs test key” and staging use case. 3) Better signposting of manual vs auto steps and expected validation lag. 4) Rate limits/quota docs need to point to where to see limits and give better 429 handling guidance. 5) Streaming session step might not be relevant for everyone and needs clearer definition.

[12:18] Sarah Kim: Yep, that’s it.

[12:20] Jordan Lee: + the mix of “capabilities” vs “must do” is confusing.

[12:24] Dev Patel: Right, add that.

[12:26] Wei Chen: On the docs side, would you prefer a single “Production defaults” page, or sprinkled into each quickstart?

[12:34] Miguel Alvarez: Single page + link from quickstarts. Otherwise people miss it. But a short snippet in the quickstart that points to it, like “for production see…”

[12:46] Sarah Kim: Yeah.

[12:47] Marissa Cole: That’s doable.

[12:49] Priya Shah: Also please add something about CORS / browser usage? We get a lot of people trying to call from frontend.

[12:56] Jordan Lee: Yep we had an intern ask if they can just call from the browser.

[13:01] Dev Patel: Ha, yeah, that’s a classic.

[13:03] Wei Chen: We can add a callout: “Use server-side only” plus how to proxy.

[13:09] Sarah Kim: That would help.

[13:11] Dev Patel: Okay. We’ve got ~30 minutes left — do you want to go deeper on any one issue? Maybe the retry/timeout specifics and what you’d consider ‘good enough’?

[13:22] Miguel Alvarez: Sure.

[13:23] Dev Patel: What are your expected workloads? Like concurrency, time budget.

[13:29] Miguel Alvarez: For interactive chat, we want first token under like 1.5 seconds and then stream. For non-stream we can tolerate like 10-15s but our infra times out at 30.

[13:42] Sarah Kim: And we may do a batch job nightly with like thousands of requests.

[13:47] Dev Patel: Okay. For interactive, streaming is the recommendation, and we should have docs that say set a connect timeout vs overall timeout. But we can give defaults.

[13:58] Priya Shah: The SDKs have different defaults right now. Python has retry built in, TS is more manual, Go has timeouts but not consistent.

[14:08] Wei Chen: Which is why the snippet parity work exists.

[14:11] Jordan Lee: Yeah we noticed that. The TS sample we used didn’t show retries.

[14:18] Marissa Cole: That’s on us.

[14:20] Dev Patel: Okay. If we provided: (a) recommended per-attempt timeout, (b) max attempts, (c) jittered exponential backoff, and (d) guidance for 429 vs 5xx — would that satisfy?

[14:33] Miguel Alvarez: Mostly yes. Also request IDs. Your support asked us for a request ID when we filed the streaming disconnect, but we didn’t know how to get it.

[14:44] Priya Shah: Yeah, the response headers include it, but the SDK should surface it.

[14:49] Wei Chen: We can add: “log x-redwood-request-id” or similar.

[14:55] Marissa Cole: The checklist could even have a “enable request IDs in logs” step in the production section.

[15:02] Sarah Kim: That’s good.

[15:04] Jordan Lee: Another thing: the checklist links open docs in a new tab and then it’s easy to lose where you were.

[15:10] Marissa Cole: Ah. The back-navigation. We heard that too. We can add a “return to checklist” banner in docs maybe with UTM.

[15:19] Wei Chen: We have a UTM convention draft but it’s not shipped.

[15:24] Dev Patel: Noted. We’ll pass that to the docs IA effort.

[15:28] Sarah Kim: Cool.

[15:30] Dev Patel: Quick question — did you manually check off any steps? Or did you assume everything was automatic?

[15:36] Jordan Lee: We assumed automatic, which is why it was confusing.

[15:40] Miguel Alvarez: Yeah we didn’t notice the “mark complete” control at first.

[15:44] Marissa Cole: Got it. That’s a UX issue.

[15:47] (crosstalk)

[15:48] Wei Chen: On “first production launch” page — did you read it? Or not yet.

[15:52] Sarah Kim: We skimmed it.

[15:54] Miguel Alvarez: It was good but it felt like a blog post. We want more checkboxes, code, do this do that.

[16:01] Wei Chen: Great, we can make it more of a runbook.

[16:04] Dev Patel: Okay.

[16:06] Dev Patel: Let’s talk streaming disconnect. You mentioned one. What happened?

[16:10] Miguel Alvarez: We were testing the TS streaming example. We got tokens, then it stopped mid-way, and our code threw an error like “connection closed.” We weren’t sure if it was our network or Redwood.

[16:23] Priya Shah: Did you see any 5xx?

[16:24] Miguel Alvarez: No, it was client exception.

[16:27] Sarah Kim: And like I said, we were on VPN.

[16:31] Priya Shah: Yeah could be network. Our guidance is: treat that as retryable if you haven’t executed side effects. But we need to be careful in docs.

[16:41] Jordan Lee: Also if you retry, you might get a different completion, which is fine but you should tell people.

[16:47] Dev Patel: Right.

[16:49] Marissa Cole: On the checklist “first streaming session” step, would you rather that be optional? Like not in the main path?

[16:56] Sarah Kim: Optional is fine. For our use case we will stream, but it shouldn’t block other folks.

[17:02] Miguel Alvarez: Or make it a “capability” section.

[17:06] Marissa Cole: Great.

[17:08] Dev Patel: Okay. I want to be mindful of time. Any other confusing step?

[17:14] Jordan Lee: The observability one. It says “visit usage analytics.” We did, and it checked off. But it doesn’t say what to look for. Like, should we set alerts? Should we export metrics?

[17:27] Sarah Kim: Yeah, like a minimum. If you say “production launch,” you should say “set up alert on error rate” or “watch 429 rate.”

[17:36] Priya Shah: + watch spend.

[17:38] Wei Chen: We can add a minimum observability list: p95 latency, error rate by status code, rate limit events, and token spend.

[17:48] Dev Patel: That maps to what SRE would want anyway.

[17:51] Miguel Alvarez: Also in the UI it would be cool if the checklist could detect that you set a webhook or something, but that’s probably later.

[17:58] Marissa Cole: Yeah Phase 1 it’s mostly doc links + a few validations.

[18:04] Dev Patel: Okay. One more question on the docs deep links: did you feel they went to the right place, or did you land in a generic doc section?

[18:13] Sarah Kim: Mostly right. There was one link that went to like an older page? I’m not sure.

[18:18] Wei Chen: Do you remember which step?

[18:20] Sarah Kim: I think it was the rate limit one.

[18:22] Wei Chen: Okay. We might have a redirect issue.

[18:26] Marissa Cole: That’s important. If you can send the URL, we’ll fix.

[18:30] Sarah Kim: Sure.

[18:32] Dev Patel: Great.

[18:34] Dev Patel: Switching gears — any comparison to other providers? Like how this onboarding felt relative to Bedrock or OpenAI.

[18:42] Jordan Lee: OpenAI is super simple but it’s also like, you know, you’re on their rails. Bedrock is painful because AWS console.

[18:51] Miguel Alvarez: Together had good quickstarts. But it lacked “what does production mean.” So this is actually better direction.

[19:00] Dev Patel: Great.

[19:02] Marissa Cole: Our goal is “simple like OpenAI” but with more production guardrails.

[19:08] Sarah Kim: Yeah.

[19:10] Dev Patel: Okay. Let’s align on concrete asks. I’ll propose a few and you tell me.

[19:16] Dev Patel: Ask 1: Add explicit step “Add retries + timeouts (recommended defaults)” near the top, right after first request. Include copy-paste SDK code.

[19:27] Miguel Alvarez: Yes.

[19:28] Sarah Kim: Yes.

[19:30] Dev Patel: Ask 2: In each auto-validated step, show “may take up to 5 minutes” and show last checked timestamp.

[19:38] Sarah Kim: Yes.

[19:39] Jordan Lee: Yes.

[19:41] Dev Patel: Ask 3: Separate sections “Capabilities” and “Production safety.” Capabilities don’t gate “First production launch.”

[19:49] Jordan Lee: Yes.

[19:50] Miguel Alvarez: Yep.

[19:52] Dev Patel: Ask 4: Rate limits step: make it earlier, link directly to quota page, and add a short explanation of 429 handling.

[19:59] Sarah Kim: Yeah.

[20:01] Priya Shah: + mention “don’t hammer refresh and re-run steps.”

[20:05] (laughter)

[20:06] Dev Patel: Yep.

[20:08] Wei Chen: On retry guidance, do you want “one size fits most” or per-workload?

[20:14] Miguel Alvarez: Give “default,” then optional tuning knobs. Like “if batch, do X.”

[20:22] Wei Chen: Got it.

[20:24] Dev Patel: Okay. We’re at ~20 minutes in. We can spend the rest on one deep dive: either production checklist definition or SDK snippet specifics. Which is more useful?

[20:35] Sarah Kim: Production checklist definition.

[20:37] Jordan Lee: + how you define “done.”

[20:40] Dev Patel: Great.

[20:42] Marissa Cole: Our current “first production launch” definition is: prod key, retries/timeouts, rate limit handling, basic monitoring, safe rollout plan, and rollback. We don’t require streaming or tool calling.

[20:56] Sarah Kim: Okay. For safe rollout, what does that mean in Hosted API? We don’t control model version maybe?

[21:03] Marissa Cole: You can pin model versions, and you can do canary by routing a percentage of traffic in your app. In Console we also have rollouts but it’s not fully integrated in Phase 1.

[21:15] Jordan Lee: That might be too advanced for onboarding.

[21:17] Dev Patel: Maybe we present a minimum: “start with 1% traffic, monitor errors, then ramp.”

[21:24] Wei Chen: And provide an example.

[21:27] Miguel Alvarez: Yeah. Also “fallback model” would be nice. Like if one model is down, route to a smaller one.

[21:35] Dev Patel: We support fallback policies, but again, maybe too advanced.

[21:39] Marissa Cole: We can mention it as recommended.

[21:43] Sarah Kim: Keep the minimum small.

[21:46] Dev Patel: Yep.

[21:48] Priya Shah: From support perspective, minimum should include: log request IDs, handle 401/429/5xx, and have a person who owns the key rotation.

[21:58] Sarah Kim: Key rotation! Good one.

[22:01] Wei Chen: We don’t have that in the doc yet.

[22:04] Marissa Cole: It’s probably a best practice, but yeah.

[22:07] Jordan Lee: At least “don’t hardcode key in repo.”

[22:10] Dev Patel: Absolutely.

[22:12] Dev Patel: Any other “must haves” you’d expect?

[22:16] Miguel Alvarez: A note on data handling. Like you say you don’t store prompts, but does telemetry include prompt text? We had internal questions.

[22:26] Dev Patel: Good question. For onboarding telemetry specifically, we’re not collecting customer prompt content. It’s event-level: “step completed” and some metadata like SDK language, but no raw prompts. We can share the privacy summary.

[22:41] Sarah Kim: That would help for our compliance folks.

[22:44] Priya Shah: We should send the security review snippet.

[22:48] Wei Chen: I’ll add a short doc note too.

[22:52] Dev Patel: Great.

[22:54] (pause)

[22:55] Dev Patel: We’re coming up on time, but I want to capture any quick UI feedback. Like the placement in Console.

[23:02] Jordan Lee: Sidebar is fine. I like that it’s not a modal.

[23:06] Sarah Kim: Agree.

[23:08] Miguel Alvarez: The progress bar is motivating, but the “stuck” feeling when it doesn’t update is real.

[23:14] Marissa Cole: Understood.

[23:16] Dev Patel: Okay, last 10 minutes: logistics. We’re planning another beta build in the next release train. Would you be open to testing again?

[23:25] Sarah Kim: Yes.

[23:26] Jordan Lee: Yep.

[23:28] Dev Patel: Cool.

[23:30] Dev Patel: To make it actionable: Sarah, can you send us the step names + any screenshots where it was confusing? Especially the 401/prod key and the lag.

[23:41] Sarah Kim: Yep I can.

[23:43] Dev Patel: Miguel, can you share your current TS wrapper for retries/timeouts? Not for us to copy, but to see what you ended up doing.

[23:51] Miguel Alvarez: Sure.

[23:53] Wei Chen: That’d be super helpful.

[23:55] Dev Patel: And we’ll send you a draft doc section for retries/timeouts. You can redline.

[24:01] Jordan Lee: Sounds good.

[24:03] Dev Patel: Anything else before we wrap?

[24:06] Sarah Kim: Just one: it’d be nice if the checklist had a “contact support” link right there, with context.

[24:12] Priya Shah: Yes, please.

[24:14] Marissa Cole: Yeah we can add “Need help?” and include the org/project ID.

[24:19] Dev Patel: Great ask.

[24:21] Dev Patel: Alright, recap:
- We’ll update step grouping: capabilities vs production safety.
- Add earlier explicit retries/timeouts step with code.
- Improve prod vs test key wording and maybe error message linking.
- Make auto vs manual obvious; show validation lag expectations.
- Improve 429/quota guidance and link to limits page.
- Share telemetry privacy summary.

[24:48] Dev Patel: Thanks everyone. We’ll follow up on email with links and next meeting options.

[24:53] Sarah Kim: Thanks.

[24:54] Miguel Alvarez: Thank you.

[24:55] Jordan Lee: Bye.

---

Auto-generated notes (may be incomplete)
Questions raised:
- What is the recommended timeout + retry policy for Hosted API (and how does it differ for streaming vs non-streaming)?
- How is “first successful request” and “first streaming session” validated and what is the expected delay?
- Does onboarding telemetry collect any prompt/content data?

End of transcript.
